```text
**Issue requirements from the Sprint 0 page**

**Where issues live and how many**
- Each member proposes at least 4 feature ideas as GitHub Issues in the team's repository. More than 4 is encouraged, and there is no upper limit.
- The backlog lives in the issue tracker, not a separate document. The sprint report links to the issues. The page states: "Issues, not a document."
- Each member's 4+ issues should include 2 small or medium features and 2 ambitious features.
- Small or medium means a change one developer could finish in roughly 1 to 1.5 weeks. Ambitious means a Sprint or more of work, and such issues will probably need to be broken down into smaller tasks.

**Required fields for every issue**
- **Title:** short, descriptive, and action-oriented.
- **Summary:** what the feature is, why it matters, and who benefits.
- **User story:** either "As a [role], I want [action] so that [outcome]" or a short scenario describing what the user does and how the system should respond.
- **Rough scope:** Small, Medium, Large, or XL, with one sentence justifying the estimate.
- **Source:** where the idea came from (issue tracker, personal use, docs gap, community request, etc.).

**Definition of a good issue**
- A feature is a user-visible or developer-visible improvement: a new capability, a significant enhancement, or a meaningful non-functional improvement such as performance, accessibility, or security.
- Think big in Sprint 0. Propose features you would actually want to use or build. Some issues may be scoped, decomposed, or merged during Sprint 1 requirements analysis.

**Labels**
- Size: `scope: small`, `scope: medium`, `scope: large`, `scope: xl`.
- Type: `type: feature` (new capability), `type: improvement` (enhances an existing capability), `type: bug` (a bug).
- Use the project's existing labels where they exist. Create these labels if they don't.

**Assignment and implementation rules (D5)**
- The instructor posts 2 to 3 issues in the first week of Sprint 0. Two or three members implement these, coordinating as a team.
- Every other member picks 2 issues from the team backlog or the project's existing tracker, limited to small or medium scope.
- Members must implement issues they did not write. No two members may implement the same issue.
- Before coding, read the issue carefully and ask the author on the issue if anything is unclear.
- Each PR must be linked to an issue in its description using `Closes #<number>`.

**Grading rules for issues**
- D2 (20 points) covers the quality, specificity, and ambition of the issues, completeness of required fields, and appropriate labels.
- Teams with exceptional backlog depth may earn up to 5 extra credit points on D2, at the instructor's discretion.
- D6 requires the report to state how many issues were created, summarize their themes, list the top 3 to 5 features the team wants to pursue, and link to the issues.
- The submission checklist requires all D2 issues to be labeled and linked from the sprint report.

**Not covered on this page**
- Issue templates, acceptance criteria, milestones, estimate points beyond the scope labels, and general assignment rules are not specified.
- The project board is not mentioned, so there are no grading rules for it.
```

```text
**Note:** The page doesn't mention labels or define point values for small, medium, or large sizes.

**Backlog refinement and decomposition (D1)**
- Review all open issues as a team. Add missing issues and close invalid or duplicate ones.
- Split large and XL issues into sub-issues that fit within the sprint. Record decisions in a team meeting or Zulip thread.
- Close or explicitly defer all Sprint 0 issues before starting Sprint 1.

**Estimation and selection (D1)**
- Size and rank issues with story points and planning poker. Any unit for story points is acceptable.
- Select only what the full team can realistically finish in about 2.5 weeks. The page advises planning conservatively and expanding if ahead of schedule.
- Minimums: each CSCI 435 member needs at least two medium issues (or equivalent points). Each CSCI 535 member needs at least two medium issues plus one additional small issue.

**Ownership and milestone (D1)**
- Every selected issue needs exactly one owner, assigned in GitHub. No issue may have more than one assignee.
- Each member owns at least one selected issue. Members may own more.
- Create a milestone named `Sprint 1` and attach all selected issues to it.
- The instructor or TA may add issues or flag priorities mid-sprint. Treat these as urgent customer requests.

**Issue content and specifications (D2)**
- The owner writes or refines the spec before writing any code.
- If the project has an issue template, adapt it. If not, create one.
- Feature issues use a user story ("As a [type of user], I want [goal] so that [benefit].") and should satisfy INVEST criteria.
- Feature issues include these sections: User Story, User Scenario, Acceptance Criteria, Out of Scope, and Open Questions.
- Each feature needs at least three acceptance criteria, each with a clear pass/fail outcome.
- Bug reports include Observed Behavior (OB), Expected Behavior (EB), and Steps to Reproduce (S2R). Additional Information (screenshots, stack traces, logs) is recommended.
- At least one teammate must comment on the issue confirming the spec is clear enough to implement.
- Suggested target: specs written and peer-reviewed by Sep 27.

**Design decisions (D3)**
- Each owner documents at least one non-trivial decision per issue, in a `## Design` section of the issue body, an issue comment, or the PR description.
- Each entry should state the decision, at least two alternatives, the rationale, and the consequences.
- Architecture-wide decisions go in `docs/sprint1/design.md`.

**Linking PRs and AI logs**
- Each PR links to its issue with `Closes #<number>`. Each issue needs at least one merged and closed PR. If an issue needs several PRs, split it into sub-issues first.
- AI log references go in issue comments, not PR descriptions. Each contributor (implementer, reviewer, estimator) posts their own comment.
- If no AI was used for an issue, post a note saying so in an issue comment.

**Sprint report (D6)**
- Link the Sprint 1 milestone and include a table listing each issue's title, owner, estimated points, scope, and status.
- Explain how the sprint was scoped.

**Grading**
- D1 (Sprint Backlog), 10 points, team: issues selected, estimated, assigned, and attached to the milestone, with rationale in the report.
- D2 (Requirements Specification), 20 points, individual: user story format, INVEST criteria, acceptance criteria quality, and peer review evidence on issues.
- D3 (Design Decisions), 7 points, individual: at least one clear, non-trivial decision per issue.
- D5 (AI Logs), 7 points, individual: logs present and linked to issues.

**Project board**
- GitHub Projects is suggested, not required. The page recommends the Team planning or Kanban template and custom fields such as estimated story points.
- The page sets no grading rules for the project board itself.
```

```text
**Issue content and process**
- Issues use user stories, acceptance criteria, and an estimate. The user story, INVEST, and acceptance-criteria rules are unchanged from Sprint 1 (D2).

- Specs must be written and peer-reviewed before coding starts (D2).

**Sizing and estimates**
- Issues are sized as small or medium, or by equivalent story points.
- Small and medium issues are mentioned, but the page doesn't define them.

**Scope minimums (D1)**
- CSCI 435 members: at least 2 medium issues, or equivalent story points.
- CSCI 535 members: at least 2 medium issues plus 1 additional small issue, or equivalent story points.

**Sprint 1 carryovers (D1)**
- Unfinished Sprint 1 issues are a priority and go into the Sprint 2 backlog before new work is selected.
- If a carryover is dropped, document the reason on the issue. Acceptable reasons are that it was closed, made invalid by later changes, or is no longer relevant.

**Breaking down and creating issues (D1)**
- If the backlog falls short of the minimums, create new issues. Look for new features, improvements, test coverage gaps, or bugs.
- New issues follow the same process: user story, acceptance criteria, and estimate.
- The instructor or TA may require specific issues or add issues to the team backlog.

**Milestones and assignment (D1, D8, checklist)**
- Create a "Sprint 2" milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues.
- Issues must be assigned.
- D8 must link to the milestone and explain backlog rationale and any carryovers or skips.

**Linking AI logs to issues (D5, "Things that must improve")**
- For any issue or PR involving AI use, post a comment that links directly to the specific log file. Folder links or links to other issues or PRs don't count.
- Logs may be referenced from either the issue or the PR.

**Diagram scope (D6)**
- The person who resolved a medium issue creates its class and sequence diagrams. Small issues equivalent to one medium issue are covered together.

**Review rules (D4, "Things that must improve")**
- No one may approve or merge their own PR.
- Reviewers must post substantive comments, not just approvals.
- Notify your reviewer promptly through Zulip or email. Aim to respond within 24 hours.

**Grading rules**
- D1 (10 points, team): issues selected, estimated, assigned, milestone created, and carryover decisions documented.
- D2 (20 points, individual): user story format, INVEST criteria, acceptance-criteria quality, and peer review evidence.
- D4 (20 points, individual): per PR, acceptance criteria (6), tests (5), description including the tech debt section (4), CI or documented manual verification (3), and a substantive review comment (2).
- Every PR description must include a Tech Debt section with "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields. "None." is accepted, but a missing section loses points.
- A team with no merged PRs receives 0 for Sprint 2.
- Upstream PRs that are accepted or under active review can earn up to 3 bonus points each, at the instructor's discretion.
```

```text
import { useHotkeys } from 'react-hotkeys-hook';
import { useLocation } from 'react-router';

import { useNavigate } from '#hooks/useNavigate';

// Modals, popovers, autocompletes and date pickers dismiss themselves on
// Escape, so backing out of the report must wait until they are closed.
function isOverlayOpen() {
  return document.querySelector('[data-popover], [role="dialog"]') !== null;
}

export function useEscapeToReportsOverview() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const location = useLocation();
  const cameFromOverview = Boolean(location.state?.goBack);

  useHotkeys(
    'escape',
    () => {
      if (cameFromOverview) {
        // Return to the dashboard the report was opened from
        void navigate(-1);
      } else {
        void navigate('/reports');
      }
    },
    {
      scopes: ['app'],
      ignoreEventWhen: e => e.defaultPrevented || isOverlayOpen(),
    },
    [navigate, cameFromOverview],
  );
}
```

````markdown
# Issue #96 rescope — drafts

Replace `#A`–`#D` with the real issue numbers once the sub-issues are filed.
Suggested order: #A first (the others depend on it); #B, #C and #D can run in parallel after that.

---

## Parent: #96 (edit existing issue)

**Title:** Warn users before leaving a report with unsaved changes

**Labels:** `scope: large`, `type: improvement`

### Summary
If you change a report's filters, date range or display options and leave without pressing **Save widget** (or **Save** on a Custom Report), Actual drops the changes without warning. This epic adds a confirmation prompt that lets users save, discard, or stay. It's split into medium sub-issues so each one fits one developer in one sprint.

### User Story
As a budget user who tweaks dashboard reports, I want to be warned before I leave a report with unsaved changes so that I don't lose my configuration by accident.

### Sub-issues
- [ ] #A — Add an unsaved-changes guard (data router + confirmation dialog) and use it on Net Worth and Cash Flow
- [ ] #B — Add the unsaved-changes guard to the Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal reports
- [ ] #C — Add the unsaved-changes guard to the Formula, Sankey, Budget Analysis, Balance Forecast and Monte Carlo reports
- [ ] #D — Warn before leaving a Custom Report with unsaved changes

### Scope
Large: 13 widget-backed report pages plus Custom Report need the guard, and making browser back/forward and sidebar navigation blockable needs a router change in `App.tsx` first.

### Source
While reviewing the goal-card widget PRs, I noticed that leaving the card without saving silently drops your changes. None of the other reports warn you either.

---

## #A — Add an unsaved-changes guard and use it on Net Worth and Cash Flow

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Estimate:** _TBD (planning poker)_

### Summary
Build the shared pieces every report will use: (1) switch the app to a React Router data router so navigation can be blocked, (2) add a reusable hook that blocks navigation while a report has unsaved changes, and (3) add a Save / Discard / Cancel dialog. Then wire it into the Net Worth and Cash Flow reports to prove it works end to end.

### User Story
As a user editing a Net Worth or Cash Flow widget, I want to be asked whether to save before I leave the page so that I don't lose filter or date-range changes by accident.

### User Scenario
1. On the dashboard, the user opens a Net Worth widget, which takes them to `/reports/net-worth/:id`.
2. They change the date range and add an account filter but don't press **Save widget**.
3. They press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, click **Budget** in the sidebar, or press the browser back button.
4. A dialog says the report has unsaved changes and offers **Save**, **Discard** and **Cancel**.
5. **Save** saves the widget and then finishes the navigation. **Discard** navigates without saving. **Cancel** closes the dialog and leaves them on the report with their edits intact.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** a Net Worth or Cash Flow widget with changes that differ from its saved settings, **when** the user presses <kbd>Esc</kbd>, uses the sidebar, or presses browser back/forward, **then** the unsaved-changes dialog appears and navigation doesn't happen until the user picks an option.
2. **Given** the dialog is open, **when** the user picks **Save**, **then** the widget is saved (a refreshed dashboard shows the new settings) and the navigation they started completes. If the save fails, they stay on the report and see an error notification.
3. **Given** the dialog is open, **when** the user picks **Discard**, **then** navigation completes and the widget's saved settings are unchanged.
4. **Given** the dialog is open, **when** the user picks **Cancel** or presses <kbd>Esc</kbd>, **then** the dialog closes, the user stays on the report, and their edits are still on screen.
5. **Given** a report with no changes, or changes that the user reverted back to the saved values, **when** the user navigates away, **then** no dialog appears.
6. **Given** a report opened without a widget (for example `/reports/net-worth`, which has no **Save widget** button), **when** the user navigates away, **then** no dialog appears.
7. **Given** unsaved changes in the browser build, **when** the user reloads or closes the tab, **then** the browser's native "Leave site?" prompt appears.
8. Existing tests still pass, and new unit tests cover the hook's dirty detection and each of the dialog's three outcomes.

### Out of Scope
- Every report other than Net Worth and Cash Flow (#B, #C, #D).
- Autosaving reports.
- Rewriting the app's routes as data-router route objects. Only the minimal wrapper described below is in scope.

### Open Questions
- In the Electron app, a `beforeunload` handler that cancels the close stops the window from closing *without showing any prompt*. Should we skip `beforeunload` in Electron, or show our own dialog through the Electron main process?
- Should switching dashboards from inside a report count as leaving? (Proposed: yes, since it's a route change.)
- On mobile the report has a back button but no **Save widget** button. Should the guard be turned off below the narrow-width breakpoint? (Proposed: yes.)

### Scope
Medium: the router switch and the shared hook/dialog are most of the work, and only two reports are wired up here.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design (draft — owner to confirm or revise)
**Decision 1: how to intercept navigation.**
- *Option A:* Use `useBlocker` with a minimal data-router wrapper: replace `<BrowserRouter>` in `App.tsx` with `createBrowserRouter([{ path: '*', element: <AppRoot /> }])` + `<RouterProvider>`, so all existing nested `<Routes>` keep working unchanged.
- *Option B:* Intercept only on-page exits: wrap the <kbd>Esc</kbd> handler in `useEscapeToReportsOverview.ts` and the back buttons. No router change, but the sidebar, browser back/forward and links aren't caught.
- *Option C:* Fully migrate every route to data-router route objects.
- *Rationale:* A covers every way of leaving with one hook and touches a single file. B leaves the most common exits unguarded. C is a large refactor unrelated to this feature.
- *Consequences:* `useBlocker` throws when it isn't inside a data router. Any test that renders a guarded report inside `<MemoryRouter>` (for example `GoalReport.test.tsx`) has to switch to `createMemoryRouter` + `<RouterProvider>`, or the hook has to be mocked. Because <kbd>Esc</kbd> already calls `navigate()`, `useBlocker` catches it with no extra code.

**Decision 2: how to detect unsaved changes.**
- *Option A:* Derive it. Each report builds the `meta` it would save with one function, used by both **Save widget** and the guard, and the guard deep-compares that against `widget.meta`.
- *Option B:* Keep a "touched" flag that every setter turns on.
- *Rationale:* A doesn't prompt when a user changes something and then changes it back, and it can't drift out of sync with what **Save** actually writes.
- *Consequences:* Each report's `onSaveWidget` has to be refactored to call a `buildWidgetMeta()` helper. #B and #C depend on this pattern.

**Proposed hook API** (publish early so #B–#D can start in parallel):
```ts
useUnsavedChangesGuard({ isDirty: boolean, onSave: () => Promise<void> })
```

---

## #B — Add the unsaved-changes guard to Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Depends on:** #A · **Estimate:** _TBD_

### Summary
Use the guard from #A on six more widget reports, so leaving any of them with unsaved changes shows the Save / Discard / Cancel dialog.

### User Story
As a user who customizes Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar or Goal widgets, I want the same unsaved-changes warning as Net Worth so that every report behaves the same and I don't lose edits.

### User Scenario
A user opens a Calendar widget, changes the date range, and clicks **Reports** in the sidebar. The dialog appears. They pick **Save**; the widget is saved and the dashboard opens with the new range.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** any of the six reports, opened from a widget, with settings that differ from the saved widget, **when** the user leaves by any route change (<kbd>Esc</kbd>, sidebar, browser back/forward), **then** the dialog from #A appears.
2. **Given** each of the six reports, **when** the user picks **Save** in the dialog, **then** the saved widget contains exactly what pressing **Save widget** would have saved (checked by a unit test per report that compares `buildWidgetMeta()` with the saved payload).
3. **Given** each of the six reports with no changes, or with changes reverted to the saved values, **when** the user leaves, **then** no dialog appears.
4. **Given** the Goal report, **when** the user only renames the widget with the inline name editor (which saves right away), **then** leaving doesn't trigger the dialog.
5. The existing tests `GoalReport.test.tsx` and `GoalCard.test.tsx` pass, updated for the data router if needed.

### Out of Scope
- The reports in #C and #D.
- Changes to the dialog or hook itself. File follow-ups against #A instead.

### Open Questions
- Spending has date/compare-mode presets that are computed from today's date. Should a widget saved as "this month" count as unsaved the next month, when the concrete dates differ? (Proposed: compare the saved preset, not the resolved dates.)

### Scope
Medium: six reports, each needing its save logic refactored into a `buildWidgetMeta()` helper plus a test. The shared work is already done in #A.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design
_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision here, for example how to compare relative or "live" date ranges (Spending, Calendar) without false positives, with at least two alternatives, the rationale and the consequences._

---

## #C — Add the unsaved-changes guard to Formula, Sankey, Budget Analysis, Balance Forecast and Monte Carlo

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Depends on:** #A · **Estimate:** _TBD_

### Summary
Use the guard from #A on the remaining widget reports. Four of them (Sankey, Budget Analysis, Balance Forecast, Monte Carlo) are experimental and only appear when their feature flag is on in **Settings → Experimental features**.

### User Story
As a user trying out the experimental reports or building Formula widgets, I want to be warned before leaving with unsaved changes so that I don't lose settings that take effort to set up, such as formulas or simulation parameters.

### User Scenario
A user turns on the Monte Carlo experimental feature, opens a Monte Carlo widget, changes the simulation inputs, and presses browser back. The dialog appears. They pick **Cancel** and stay on the report with their inputs intact.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** any of the five reports, opened from a widget, with settings that differ from the saved widget, **when** the user leaves by any route change, **then** the dialog from #A appears.
2. **Given** a Formula widget, **when** the user edits the formula text without saving and leaves, **then** the dialog appears. **When** they pick **Save**, **then** the new formula is saved.
3. **Given** Balance Forecast or Monte Carlo, which already write to `widget.meta` in more than one place, **when** the user picks **Save**, **then** settings saved earlier in the session aren't overwritten with stale values (covered by a unit test).
4. **Given** each of the five reports with no changes, **when** the user leaves, **then** no dialog appears.
5. **Given** a report whose feature flag is off, **then** nothing about the app's behavior changes.

### Out of Scope
- Reports covered by #B and #D.
- Taking any report out of experimental status.

### Open Questions
- Monte Carlo results are computed and can be expensive. Do any computed values end up in `meta`, and should they be left out of the comparison? (Proposed: compare only user inputs.)

### Scope
Medium: five reports. Formula, Balance Forecast and Monte Carlo have more complex `meta` than the reports in #B, and the feature flags need extra manual testing.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design
_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision, for example how to handle reports whose `meta` is updated from more than one code path, with alternatives, rationale and consequences._

---

## #D — Warn before leaving a Custom Report with unsaved changes

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Depends on:** #A · **Estimate:** _TBD_

### Summary
Custom Reports don't use **Save widget**. They have their own save menu, and they already track whether a saved report has been modified (`savedStatus` is `'saved' | 'new' | 'modified'` in `SaveReportMenu.tsx`). Hook that status into the guard from #A, including the case where the user wants to save a report that has never been saved and therefore has no name yet.

### User Story
As a user building a Custom Report, I want to be warned before I leave with unsaved changes so that I don't lose a report I spent time configuring.

### User Scenario
1. A user opens a saved Custom Report, changes the grouping from Category to Payee (the header now shows the report as modified), and clicks **Accounts** in the sidebar.
2. The dialog appears. They pick **Save**, the report is updated, and the Accounts page opens.
3. Next they start a new Custom Report, configure it, and press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. The dialog appears. **Save** opens the existing "name this report" prompt, and once they confirm a name the report is saved and navigation continues.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** a Custom Report with `savedStatus === 'modified'`, **when** the user leaves by any route change, **then** the dialog from #A appears. **Save** updates the existing saved report and then navigation continues.
2. **Given** a new, never-saved Custom Report that the user has changed from the defaults, **when** they leave and pick **Save**, **then** the name prompt opens. Confirming saves the report and continues navigation; cancelling the prompt keeps them on the report.
3. **Given** a Custom Report with `savedStatus === 'saved'`, or a new report still on its default settings, **when** the user leaves, **then** no dialog appears.
4. **Given** the dialog is open, **when** the user picks **Discard**, **then** navigation continues and the saved report in the database is unchanged.

### Out of Scope
- Changing how Custom Report keeps its in-progress state in session storage (`setSessionReport`).
- Widget-backed reports (#A–#C).

### Open Questions
- Should a new report count as "changed from defaults" if the user only changed the date range? (Needs agreement before implementation.)
- Because Custom Report keeps unsaved state in session storage, the user's edits may already be restored when they come back. Should **Discard** also clear the session state, so it really discards?

### Scope
Medium: dirty detection already exists, but the "Save" path has to handle both updating an existing report and naming a brand-new one from inside the dialog.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design
_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision, for example how **Save** from the dialog reuses the existing `SaveReport` name flow versus adding a name field to the dialog, with alternatives, rationale and consequences._
````

```markdown
# Issue #96 rescope — drafts

Replace `#A` and `#B` with the real issue numbers once the sub-issues are filed.
Do #A first. #B reuses the helper that #A adds.

---

## Parent: #96 (edit existing issue)

**Title:** Show when a report widget has unsaved changes

**Labels:** `scope: large`, `type: improvement`

### Summary
When you change a report's filters, date range or display options and then leave without pressing **Save widget**, Actual drops the changes, and nothing on the page tells you they were unsaved. Custom Reports already show "(modified)" next to the report name when they have unsaved edits; the other 13 dashboard widget reports don't. This epic adds the same "(modified)" label to every widget report, so users can see at a glance that they have something to save.

### User Story
As a budget user who customizes dashboard reports, I want to see when a report has unsaved changes so that I remember to press **Save widget** before leaving.

### Sub-issues
- [ ] #A — Show a "(modified)" label on the standard report widgets
- [ ] #B — Show a "(modified)" label on the Formula and experimental report widgets

### Scope
Large as a whole: 13 report pages each need their own change detection. It's split into two medium sub-issues.

### Source
While reviewing the goal-card widget PRs, I noticed that leaving the card without saving silently drops your changes. None of the other reports warn you either.

### Design
**Decision: show that changes are unsaved, instead of blocking the user from leaving.**

The original version of this issue proposed a "Save / Discard / Cancel" dialog that would appear whenever the user tried to leave a report with unsaved changes. We considered three options:

- *Option A: block every way of leaving.* This would catch the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key, sidebar links, the browser back/forward buttons and closing the tab, using React Router's `useBlocker`. The catch is that `useBlocker` only works with React Router's newer "data router" setup, and `App.tsx` currently sets up routing with `<BrowserRouter>`. We would first have to change how `App.tsx` sets up routing for the entire app, not just reports.
- *Option B: block only the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key and the page's own back controls.* This needs no change to `App.tsx`, but it misses the sidebar and the browser back button, which are the most common ways to leave a page.
- *Option C (chosen): don't block at all.* Show a "(modified)" label next to the widget name while its settings differ from what's saved, matching what Custom Reports already do.

**Rationale.** Option A meant restructuring `App.tsx`, the root of the whole app. That change would affect every page, break existing tests that render components with `<MemoryRouter>`, and have to be finished before any report work could start, so one stalled PR could block the whole team. That's a lot of risk for a small feature, and Actual's maintainers would be unlikely to accept an app-wide routing change made for this reason. A blocking dialog also gets in the way of normal use: people often open a report just to look something up, change the dates, and leave without wanting to save. Option C needs no change to `App.tsx`, doesn't interrupt anyone, and matches behavior users already know from Custom Reports.

**Consequences.**
- Users can still leave without saving. The label tells them, but nothing stops them.
- The browser back button and closing the tab are not covered. If users ask for a real "are you sure?" prompt later, the routing change in `App.tsx` can be revisited as its own issue.
- The change-detection helper built in #A is reusable, so any future prompt would only need to add the dialog.

---

## #A — Show a "(modified)" label on the standard report widgets

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Estimate:** 6 points

### Summary
Add a shared way for a report to tell whether its current settings differ from the saved widget, and a "(modified)" label that matches the one Custom Reports use. Wire both into eight reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal.

### User Story
As a user who edits Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar or Goal widgets, I want to see a "(modified)" label when my changes aren't saved so that I know to press **Save widget** before leaving.

### User Scenario
1. On the dashboard, the user opens a Net Worth widget.
2. They change the date range. "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
3. They change the date range back to the saved value. The label disappears.
4. They add an account filter. The label reappears. They press **Save widget**, and the label disappears again.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** any of the eight reports opened from a widget, **when** the user changes a setting that **Save widget** would save, **then** "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
2. **Given** a report showing "(modified)", **when** the user presses **Save widget** and the save succeeds, **then** the label disappears. If the save fails, the label stays.
3. **Given** a report showing "(modified)", **when** the user changes every setting back to its saved value, **then** the label disappears.
4. **Given** a report opened without a widget (for example `/reports/net-worth`, which has no **Save widget** button), **then** the label never appears.
5. **Given** the Goal report, **when** the user only renames the widget with the inline name editor (which saves right away), **then** the label does not appear.
6. Each of the eight reports has a unit test showing that the settings checked for changes are exactly the settings **Save widget** writes.

### Out of Scope
- The Formula and experimental reports (#B).
- Custom Reports, which already have this label.
- Any dialog or prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router (see the Design section in #96).

### Open Questions
- Spending and Calendar can use relative date ranges such as "this month". Should a widget saved as "this month" show as modified next month, when the actual dates have moved? (Proposed: no. Compare the saved range setting, not the dates it resolves to.)
- Should **Save widget** be disabled when there are no changes? (Proposed: no. Leave it as it is, to keep this change small and unsurprising.)

### Scope
Medium: building the shared helper and label is a small part of the work. Most of it is reworking each of the eight reports so the same function builds both what **Save widget** saves and what gets compared, plus a test per report.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design
_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision, with at least two alternatives, the rationale and the consequences. For example, how to detect changes: compare the current settings against the saved widget, or set a "touched" flag whenever a setting changes._

---

## #B — Show a "(modified)" label on the Formula and experimental report widgets

**Labels:** `scope: medium`, `type: improvement` · **Parent:** #96 · **Depends on:** #A · **Estimate:** 4 points

### Summary
Use the helper and label from #A on the five remaining widget reports: Formula, Sankey, Budget Analysis, Balance Forecast and Monte Carlo. The last four are experimental and only appear when their feature flag is on in **Settings → Experimental features**.

### User Story
As a user building Formula widgets or trying the experimental reports, I want to see a "(modified)" label when my changes aren't saved so that I don't lose settings that took effort to set up, such as formulas or simulation inputs.

### User Scenario
A user turns on the Monte Carlo experimental feature and opens a Monte Carlo widget. They change the simulation inputs, and "(modified)" appears next to the widget name. They press **Save widget**, and the label disappears.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. **Given** any of the five reports opened from a widget, **when** the user changes a setting that **Save widget** would save, **then** "(modified)" appears next to the widget name. Saving successfully, or changing the setting back, removes it.
2. **Given** a Formula widget, **when** the user edits the formula text without saving, **then** the label appears.
3. **Given** Balance Forecast or Monte Carlo, which write to the saved widget from more than one place in their code, **when** one of those other saves happens, **then** the label reflects the newly saved settings and is not stuck on "(modified)". A unit test covers this.
4. **Given** a report whose feature flag is off, **then** nothing about the app's behavior changes.

### Out of Scope
- The reports covered by #A.
- Taking any report out of experimental status.
- Any dialog or prompt when leaving the page.

### Open Questions
- Monte Carlo computes results that may be stored with the widget. Should computed values be left out of the comparison, so only the user's inputs count as changes? (Proposed: yes.)

### Scope
Medium: only five reports and the pattern already exists from #A, but Formula, Balance Forecast and Monte Carlo store more complicated settings than the reports in #A, and each experimental report needs its feature flag turned on to test.

### Source
Split out of #96.

### Design
_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision, with at least two alternatives, the rationale and the consequences. For example, how to keep the label correct when a report saves to its widget from more than one place._
```

_**User (2026-10-27 21:53:17Z)**_

On github, sometimes a description will just show #125, but other times it shows #125 --- the title. Why?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 21:53:29Z)**_

It depends on where the reference sits. GitHub shows the issue's title (and an open/closed icon) only when the reference is the only thing in a list item:

```markdown
- #125                     → shows "#125 Show a (modified) label on …" with a status icon
- [ ] #125                 → same, as a checklist item
See #125 for details.      → just a plain "#125" link
- #125 — some extra text   → usually just "#125" plus your text
```

Anywhere else, such as inside a sentence, a heading or a table, it stays a plain `#125` link, and you see the title only when you hover over it.

**How this affects the drafts:** #96's sub-issue checklist currently has the title typed out after each placeholder (`- [ ] #A — Show a "(modified)" label…`). Once the sub-issues are filed, I'd change those lines to just the number:

```markdown
- [ ] #125
- [ ] #126
```

GitHub then fills in the titles and shows whether each issue is open or closed, and they stay correct if someone renames an issue. If you also add them as sub-issues of #96 with GitHub's sub-issue button, they appear in their own panel with a progress bar as well.
